div.head: Wl art retr Inscr.
div.ab: Decreta domini regis Willelmi bastardi et emendaciones, quas posuit in Anglia, que olim uocabatur Britannia. ¶ Hic etiam intimatur, quid Willelmus rex Anglorum cum principibus suis constituit post conquisicionem Anglie.
[Carta regis Willelmi conquisitoris de quibusdam statutis etc.] ¶ Willelmus rex Anglorum dux Normannorum omnibus hominibus suis Francis et Anglis salutem.
Decreta domini regis Willelmi bastardi et emendaciones quas posuit in Anglia quae olim vocabatur Britannia. Hic eciam intimatur &c.
The decrees and legal reforms of our lord King William the Bastard, which he established in England, formerly called Britain. Notice is hereby given &c.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 244–245 (text and translation); Robertson prints only the clauses that differ from Wl art: for 3.1–4, 10 and 12–15 she refers the reader to Wl art 3.1–4, 5 and 6–9.; Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 489, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c. 1210 (Robertson)”, now “c.1210 (Liebermann, Robertson)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.1210 (Liebermann, Robertson)”, now “c. 1210 (Liebermann, I p. 489)”); V: page of the modern editor’s text / translation, checked against Robertson (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “244”, now “244 / 245”; 14 rows of Wl art retr)
